intent: The centered modal popup of an AlertDialog, portalled above a dimming backdrop, holding the question and its two answers.
typical_uses: The panel carrying a confirmation's title, its consequence and the confirm and cancel actions

dont_use_when.situation: A modal panel holding a form or other content the user works in
A panel anchored beside a trigger rather than centered over the page

invariants.text: The popup and its backdrop are in the DOM only while the alert dialog is open or animating closed; the kit passes no `keepMounted` to the portal, so a closed alert dialog renders nothing.

Without `container`, the popup portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the popup only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.

The popup takes its accessible name from the AlertDialogTitle inside it and its description from the AlertDialogDescription, through `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`; without a title, pass `aria-label` on AlertDialogContent.
Unless `initialFocus` says otherwise, opening moves focus to the first tabbable element inside the popup, or to the popup itself when it holds none or the dialog was opened by touch.
With `showBackdrop={false}` the primitive still renders a transparent backdrop of its own, because an alert dialog is always modal, so the page behind stays blocked.

`size` is stamped on the popup as `data-size`. Below 640px the popup is capped at 20rem, or at the viewport width minus var(--space-8) when that is narrower. At `default` it widens to a 32rem cap from 640px, where the footer lines its actions up at the end of one row; below 640px the footer stacks them with the last one on top. At `sm` the popup stays capped at 20rem at every width, and the footer lays out two equal columns.

The popup's height is capped at the viewport height minus var(--space-8) and it scrolls its own content past that. The popup carries no padding: the inset sits on its direct children, and a `className` setting padding on one of them replaces that inset rather than adding to it.
The popup fades and scales on open and close; under `prefers-reduced-motion` alert-dialog.module.css drops the transform transition and keeps the fade.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Always render an AlertDialogTitle, hidden visually through `className` when the design shows none, so the popup has an accessible name

a11y.by: the primitive's Dialog.Popup sets role `alertdialog`; alert-dialog.test.tsx asserts the open popup is found by role `alertdialog` and that an outside press leaves it open

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the popup portals into; an explicit null renders no popup until a node is passed
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

initialFocus.states: initialFocus picks the element focused on open - true for the first tabbable element (the popup itself when opened by touch), false for no move, a ref to an element, or a function of the opening interaction type
initialFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` - a ref object and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

finalFocus.states: finalFocus picks the element focused on close - true for the trigger or the previously focused element, false for no move, a ref to an element, or a function of the closing interaction type
finalFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` - a ref object and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the popup's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the popup's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, nested, transitionStatus, nestedDialogOpen). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through alert-dialog.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside AlertDialogContent; only its `container` is exposed, as AlertDialogContent's own prop.
Composed inside AlertDialogContent and rendered unless `showBackdrop` is false; it takes no props from the caller.

good.title: A narrow confirmation with side-by-side actions
good.code:
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger>Sign out</AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent size="sm">
    <AlertDialogHeader>
      <AlertDialogTitle>Sign out of every device?</AlertDialogTitle>
    </AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogFooter>
      <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
      <AlertDialogAction onClick={signOutEverywhere}>Sign out</AlertDialogAction>
    </AlertDialogFooter>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>

good.title: A popup portalled into a themed subtree

bad.title: Content with no AlertDialog root around it
bad.why: The primitive's Portal and Popup read the nearest AlertDialog root's state through context and throw when there is none.

capabilities.name: backdrop
capabilities.description: Default true: a fixed layer behind the popup dims the page with the var(--overlay-modal) scrim and fades in and out with it.

container.typeText: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null | undefined

container.description: Partially typed: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property and none for this one; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.partially_typed_props. container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the popup portals into; an explicit null renders no popup until a node is passed. `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

finalFocus.description: TS: boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType: InteractionType) => boolean | void | HTMLElement | null) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. finalFocus picks the element focused on close - true for the trigger or the previously focused element, false for no move, a ref to an element, or a function of the closing interaction type. `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` - a ref object and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

initialFocus.description: TS: boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType: InteractionType) => boolean | void | HTMLElement | null) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. initialFocus picks the element focused on open - true for the first tabbable element (the popup itself when opened by touch), false for no move, a ref to an element, or a function of the opening interaction type. `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` - a ref object and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, DialogPopupState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the popup's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: DialogPopupState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the popup's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, nested, transitionStatus, nestedDialogOpen). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through alert-dialog.module.css, not through this.
